items.performers: Orchestra Sinfonica Nazionale della RAI, Turin; Arturo Tamayo
items.label: Mode Records, mode 299
items.note: The first recording of the original version of Metastaseis, scored for sixty-five players with fifty-two string parts. The version played in 1955, listed by Boosey & Hawkes as version B, has forty-six. Boosey & Hawkes’s video plays this performance over the publisher’s score. The Mode disc also holds Terretektorh and Nomos Gamma, recorded at the 2011 Holland Festival with the orchestra among the audience.

items.label: Timpani
items.note: Forty-six divided strings, two trombones and a percussionist. Xenakis’s note for the work lists glissandi, pizzicati, col legno and blows on the bodies of the instruments. The orchestra’s YouTube channel carries this track from the 2008 Timpani release, which also holds Metastaseis, Achorripsis and ST/48.

items.performers: Les Percussions de Strasbourg: Minh-Tâm Nguyen, Alexandre Esperet, François Papirer, Thibaut Weber, Hsin-Hsuan Wu, Yi-Ping Yang
items.label: Percussions de Strasbourg
items.note: For six percussionists; the Percussions de Strasbourg gave the first performance at Persepolis. The ensemble issued this recording on its own label with Pléiades in January 2022. Persephassa takes 29 minutes. Jean Geoffroy, who directed the recording, writes that it places the listener at the centre of the six sets, and recommends headphones. The teaser video has excerpts from both works.

items.label: Mode Records, mode 98/99
items.note: Made on the UPIC for the Polytope de Mycenae, and Xenakis’s first work made entirely of computer-generated sound. It opens a two-disc set that documents UPIC works from the CCMIX studio in Paris, with the Polytope de Cluny and pieces by Risset, Estrada, Roads, Pape and others, and a 56-page book.
